title: Worst-case transport and light cones for quasi-periodic operators
description: We study the fastest transport exponent α_u^+ of supercritical analytic quasi-periodic Schrödinger operators at the worst phase. For finite Liouville exponent β, an upper law involving the Lyapunov exponent ℓ and acceleration ω keeps transport below one uniformly in phase. When β ≥ ℓ its local rate is 1 − ℓ/(2ωβ), and the factor 2ω is attained. For the almost Mathieu operator with L = log λ > 0, we prove the sharper uniform upper bound 1 − L/(2β) also on L/2 < β < L. Thus whenever the even-denominator exponent satisfies β_e = β > L/2, with β finite, the uniform exponent, the supremum over phases and the exponent at phase 1/4 all equal 1 − L/(2β). The same value holds on a dense G_δ set, while almost every phase has max{0, 1 − L/β}. The new upper proof uses translated one-band and two-band frames, an exact inverse-Morse factorization, matrix shells and one fixed energy unit through the full depth range. For odd-harmonic analytic potentials, a half-period sign flip gives a lower bound through a closed central gap. In the Aubry–André XY chain, for even sources and the specified receivers, the fixed-site light cone follows the typical law at almost every phase; the light cone uniform over sites follows the exact worst-case law when β_e = β > L/2 is finite. For an explicit computable chain these exponents differ and both have Turing degree 0″. We also prove computability of the Lyapunov exponent for computable analytic potentials and a transport exponent of degree 0″ throughout an explicit computable even-potential neighborhood. No computation enters the new upper proof.
